subject: Clarification: SLO measurement methodology and regional weighting (OrionCorp RFP)
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@orioncorp.com>
To: procurement@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orioncorp.com
Date: 2028-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP Sec 4 — SLO measurement clarifications

Hi Redwood team,

Thanks for the RFP submission so far. We have a couple of clarification requests on section 4 (SLOs, measurement, and credits) before our evaluation committee meets next week:

1) Measurement sources — please confirm whether your SLO calculations use only provider-side telemetry, or a hybrid model that incorporates customer-side synthetic probes and/or application telemetry. If hybrid, explain reconciliation and precedence rules.
2) Regional aggregation — our traffic is globally distributed. How do you handle region-level outages vs global SLOs? Provide an example calculation for a 3-region weighting (NA/EU/APAC) with differing traffic percentages.
3) Sampling and percentiles — we need the exact percentile definitions (e.g., p50/p95/p99 on request latency: which latency bucket counts as ‘failed’?) and the sampling window used for percentiles.
4) Service credit formula — show a worked example (monthly invoice $X) for a customer whose availability in a billing month fell into your 99.5–99.0% bracket.
5) Auditability — what artifacts (logs, traces, probe data) will be provided during a dispute, and what is your retention window?

Attached: Orion_RFP_Sec4_SLOs.pdf (annotated questions inline). Please reply by COB Oct 5 as our technical evaluation is timeboxed.

Regards,
Maria Gonzalez
Senior Procurement Manager
OrionCorp
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@orioncorp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-02T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP Sec 4 — SLO measurement clarifications

Maria —

Appreciate the clear set of questions. We can meet the COB Oct 5 deadline and have attached a concise measurement spec and an example calculation workbook to make the math transparent. Summary answers below; see attachments for full detail. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you prefer to walk through the examples.

Quick summary:
- Measurement sources: hybrid approach. Primary measurement is provider-side telemetry (ingestion, inference success, per-request latency) with an optional customer-side synthetic probe input that can be used for dispute reconciliation. Provider telemetry is the default source for billing and automated SLO evaluation; customer probes are treated as independent evidence and can trigger a formal audit if discrepancies exceed thresholds.
- Reconciliation rules: provider telemetry has precedence for day-to-day SLO enforcement. If customer probe data shows >0.5% divergence for a rolling 72-hour window, we open an audit and run a reconciliation where both data sets are compared after normalizing for timezone/endpoints and sampling.
- Regional aggregation: we compute both per-region SLOs and a traffic-weighted global SLO. Example in attachment: NA 60% traffic, EU 30%, APAC 10% — global availability = sum(region_avail * weight). We also support contractual region-level SLOs if you want separate credits per region.
- Percentiles and sampling: latency percentiles are computed on successful requests only; failed requests count toward availability (i.e., availability denominator includes all true requests). We compute p50/p95/p99 on a 1-minute rolling window and then aggregate to the daily percentile using weighted histograms to avoid sample bias.
- Service credits: credits are calculated as % of monthly service fee as outlined in the attached spreadsheet — we included a worked example for 99.5%–99.0% availability.
- Auditability and retention: logs and request-level telemetry retained for 90 days by default; extended retention (1 year) available as an add-on. Audit artifacts provided include raw request logs (CSV stub), probe traces, and our aggregated SLO calculation notebook. We can provide SOC 2 summary artifact on request.

Attachments: redwood_slo_measurement_spec_v1.pdf, slo_calculation_example.xlsx

Next steps: If you want a region-level SLA (separate credits per region) vs a single global SLA, let us know — we can propose language for the RFP addendum.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Success — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Lauren —

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups from the technical reviewers:

- The reconciliation threshold (0.5% divergence) — is that absolute or relative? We need the precise calculation (difference in availability percentage points vs relative percent difference).
- For percentile aggregation, can you include the exact histogram bin sizes and explain how you avoid bias when traffic volume varies by region?
- For the audit, will Redwood provide a signed attestation that the provider telemetry used for billing is immutable for the billing window (e.g., no retroactive reclassification of failures after month close)?

Also, one of our architects asked whether Redwood supports rolling-window SLOs (e.g., 30-day rolling window) in addition to calendar-month windows for crediting purposes.

Would you be able to share a sample output of the ‘‘monthly SLO report’’ for an example month (redacted request ids okay) showing per-region rows and the final credit calculation? That will speed our legal team review.

Regards,
Maria
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@orioncorp.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-04T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP Sec 4 — SLO measurement clarifications (technical follow-ups)

Maria —

Quick technical clarifications from our side:

1) Divergence threshold: the 0.5% figure is absolute percentage points (i.e., if provider availability = 99.90% and customer probe availability = 99.35%, absolute divergence = 0.55pp -> triggers audit). We compute availability as: availability = 1 - (failed_requests / total_requests) over the evaluation window.

2) Histogram bins and percentile aggregation: we maintain fixed exponential bins for latency aggregation (0-5ms, 5-10ms, 10-25ms, 25-50ms, 50-100ms, 100-250ms, 250-500ms, 500-1000ms, >1000ms). Each server records per-minute histograms which are then merged using count-weighted summation to compute p50/p95/p99 on the merged histogram. This avoids bias from varying sample counts across regions because the merge is count-aware.

3) Immutability and audit artifacts: we persist raw request logs in append-only storage for the billing window plus retention. Operationally we take a snapshot at month-close (T+0) and compute SLOs on that snapshot. Retroactive reclassification can occur only in the case of a documented bug; any recomputation after month-close is recorded and reported to customers with explanation and an audit trail. We can provide a signed attestation that the month-close snapshot is the canonical basis for the initial invoice and crediting calculation.

4) Rolling-window support: yes — we support both calendar-month and rolling N-day windows for evaluations. For credits we default to calendar-month (to align with billing), but we can include rolling-window language in contract addenda where required.

Example calculation (high-level):

- NA weight = 0.60, EU = 0.30, APAC = 0.10
- NA availability = 99.85% (failed 225 / total 150000)
- EU availability = 99.60% (failed 120 / total 30000)
- APAC availability = 98.90% (failed 110 / total 10000)
- Weighted global avail = (0.60*99.85 + 0.30*99.60 + 0.10*98.90) = 99.526% -> rounds to 99.53% for credit bracket calculations

We will include a redacted sample monthly report as an attachment in our next email (CSV + PDF).

—Karthik
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
